cockpit_architecture.summary: Projection-driven architecture. Frontend consumes backend projections via WebSocket (local) or pywebview bridge (HTTPS/WSS). All policy decisions reside in backend. Frontend is a dumb renderer that displays projection fields and sends intent envelopes. State ownership: backend is authoritative; frontend is projection consumer. Intent model: frontend submits structured intent envelopes; backend evaluates via GovernanceEngine and returns results. Widget system: 3 disclosure levels (compact chips, standard cards, expanded full-page). Layout modes: Operator, Review, System, Technical.
how_cockpit_talks_to_backend: CockpitAPI class (read-only fallback via JS bridge)
how_intents_are_authorized: frontend builds intent envelope from user action
intent envelope sent via WebSocket/bridge to backend
frontend renders decision — never interprets or overrides
how_widgets_get_evidence_links: each widget payload includes source artifact refs (paths + SHA256)
widgets render evidence links as clickable references to JSONL artifacts
evidence links are verified by backend projection layer before inclusion in widget payload

required_status_indicators.description: Cockpit must distinguish and display these status indicators. Currently, NONE are implemented in the frontend.

indicators.what_it_means: Product telemetry is opted out. Adaptive recommendations, UX optimization, agent-tool optimization, Ralph refinement, orchestrator behavior, and subagent behavior are degraded. Local operational evidence, receipts, audit logs, and enterprise evidence are unaffected.
indicators.cockpit_display: Persistent chip/icon in header or status bar; tooltip explains degradation scope

indicators.what_it_means: Remote telemetry contribution is disabled. Local operational evidence and enterprise audit evidence remain active. Product intelligence and hosted sharing are unavailable.
indicators.cockpit_display: Separate indicator from product_telemetry_disabled; tooltip clarifies remote vs local distinction

indicators.what_it_means: Local operational observability (permission probes, health checks, receipt records) is degraded or unavailable. Governance and evidence continuity may be impacted.
indicators.cockpit_display: Warning chip; action prompt to investigate or restart

indicators.what_it_means: Enterprise audit/evidence substrate is unavailable. Required for enterprise compliance. May indicate storage failure or configuration issue.
indicators.cockpit_display: Critical warning; block mutation operations; surface admin action required

indicators.what_it_means: PostgreSQL operational substrate is not reachable. Fallback to local JSONL artifacts only. Cockpit projections may be stale. Enterprise features degraded.
indicators.cockpit_display: Warning chip; show 'Postgres unavailable — using local evidence only' message

indicators.what_it_means: GitHub API rate-limit budget is exhausted or near exhaustion. GitHub data freshness is degraded. Security/audit paths prioritized.
indicators.cockpit_display: Warning chip with remaining budget; defer non-critical GitHub data refresh

indicators.what_it_means: Last GitHub App permission probe is older than configured TTL. Current permission state may not reflect reality. Mutation operations blocked or require re-probe.
indicators.cockpit_display: Warning chip; block mutation; show 'Re-probe permissions' action button

indicators.what_it_means: GitHub Provider Trust Spine v1 prerequisites are not all satisfied. Broad GitHub surface expansion is blocked. Only read-only low-risk surfaces available.
indicators.cockpit_display: Info chip on affected panels; blocked panels show 'trust spine incomplete' message

indicators.what_it_means: Hosted/team deployment mode is not available. Running in local-only mode. Team features disabled.
indicators.cockpit_display: Info chip in admin/settings panel; show 'local-only mode' badge

surface_blocking_rules.description: These surfaces must remain disabled or degraded until their prerequisites are met.

rules.blocked_until: GitHub Provider Trust Spine v1 complete (permission probe, rate-limit budget, content-light scan, webhook HMAC verification)
content-light leak scanning proven for secret-bearing GitHub data
content-light leak scanning proven for Actions log bodies
trust spine + dry-run/rehearsal + approval receipts + branch protection preflight + no-surprise-mutation tests
Postgres + tenant isolation + RBAC + audit evidence continuity proven
no-unreviewed-generated-comments tests passing + content policy scan for PR comments

csp_xss_posture.current: Static docs use CSP header (default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; frame-ancestors 'none'). Cockpit runs in pywebview with local HTTPS. WSS connection is localhost-only with self-signed cert.
csp_xss_posture.gaps: No CSP audit for pywebview-rendered content; pywebview's web engine may have different CSP behavior than browsers; no automated XSS testing for cockpit widgets; no Content-Security-Policy header on WebSocket upgrade path; static docs CSP does not include connect-src restriction for WebSocket

projection_freshness.current: Projection is rebuilt on refresh_project intent or periodic interval. Widgets show data as-at projection build time. No per-data-source freshness tracking.
projection_freshness.gaps: No TTL per data source (GitHub alerts vs. repo metadata vs. permission probe); no stale data indicator in cockpit widgets; no forced refresh on permission probe completion; no freshness degradation warning
